sentences.transcript: Homebound, from anthology a Massachusetts poet, edited by William Stanley Bratowate.
All Libravox recordings are in the public domain.
For more information or to volunteer, please visit Libravox .org.
The moon is a wavering rim where one fish slips.
The water makes a quietness of sound.
Night is an anchoring of many ships, homebound.
There are strange tunnelers in the dark and whores of wings that die, and hairy spiders bend the silence into nets and tinnators move softly in.
I step on shadows riding through the grass and feel the night lean cool against my face, and challenged by the Sentinel of Space, I pass.
In the poem, this recording is in the public domain.
